content.text:
**Bearish-on-MCP views (e.g., Jasper Lu and related discussions):**[[1]](https://x.com/lu__jasper/status/2085117746686083226)[[1]](https://x.com/lu__jasper/status/2085117746686083226)

- **Jasper Lu (@lu__jasper)**, X post August 5, 2026 (https://x.com/lu__jasper/status/2085117746686083226): “I was already bearish on MCPs after playing around with custom agent harnesses. But after seeing these results [referencing Prime Agent], I’m convinced MCPs and custom tools were an expensive mistake. These models.. all they want to do is write code. Anything else goes against their nature and sacrifices quality. Tool calls as code are the way to go.” He highlights issues like poor composition of tool calls, exporting results (requiring re-emission of tokens), and retrying code execution via tools (forcing re-emission of full code). He contrasts this with REPL/CLI-style harnesses that store code in files/variables for in-place editing and loops for orchestration (fewer tokens, more natural).[[2]](https://x.com/lu__jasper/status/2085249778242224634)

- **Matt Shumer (@mattshumer_)** (quoted in Lu’s thread, original post from 2025 but referenced in 2026 context): Advocates converting MCP specs into code functions so the model writes code to call them instead of standard tool-calling. “Models have seen FAR more code than they have tool calls... code can orchestrate calls in more complex ways... for example, instead of doing 50 calls... a model can just write a for loop... with way fewer tokens.”[[2]](https://x.com/lu__jasper/status/2085249778242224634)

Related recent X activity echoes this, with users noting MCP hype drove open APIs but code-native approaches (e.g., REPL harnesses) are superior for agentic workflows.[[3]](https://x.com/lu__jasper/status/2086099476549112205)

**Counter-arguments from MCP proponents (token efficiency, registries, security, composability):**[[4]](https://x.com/RhysSullivan/status/2080117243405635832)[[5]](https://x.com/HiddenBrains/status/2088256828568437153)

- **Rhys Sullivan (@RhysSullivan)**, X post ~July 23, 2026 (https://x.com/RhysSullivan/status/2080117243405635832): “There’s basically no difference in the effectiveness of MCP and CLIs + skills for agents... CLIs are fine, but require basically a full sandbox... they’re also lossy—you can’t know without running a CLI what operations it contains... you also need skills with a CLI because you have to teach the agent how to use it, whereas with MCP you can do tool search. Your users want both.” Emphasizes MCP’s discoverability (registries/tool search), reduced need for custom teaching, and lighter sandboxing vs. full CLI execution environments.[[4]](https://x.com/RhysSullivan/status/2080117243405635832)

- Discussions on **security and controlled access**: MCP enables scoped/identity-based tool lists (only load needed tools to reduce context bloat), authorization checks, client identity verification, and downstream side-effect controls. Examples include on-chain rules for agent wallets (per-tx/daily limits, permissions) and interceptors blocking dangerous commands/.env reads. Proponents argue this provides structured governance that pure code-writing lacks.[[6]](https://x.com/Mattjgale87/status/2088438982652654046)[[7]](https://x.com/BLOCVENCHAINCAP/status/2088312443340542235)

- **Token efficiency and composability via scoping/registries**: MCP servers can be scoped (e.g., groups of tools instead of full server load) for 80-90% context reduction in live setups. Registries enable discoverability and composability (plug-and-play across agents/clients without hand-wiring). One post notes MCP turns agents into “extensible engineering platforms” with plugins for codebase intelligence, search, memory, etc.[[5]](https://x.com/HiddenBrains/status/2088256828568437153)[[8]](https://x.com/zooper_man/status/2086821786856165771)

- Broader ecosystem views (e.g., blog/Medium posts from mid-2026) highlight MCP as standardizing integration (discovery, schemas, approval) beyond raw function calling, with security/composability benefits for production agents.[[9]](https://medium.com/@ageddes75/i-spent-2500-hours-building-ai-agents-mcp-servers-and-developer-tools-heres-everything-i-made-a32f4e0c2d04)

**Experiments/benchmarks comparing code-execution agents vs. MCP tool-calling agents (past ~30 days or recent 2026 context):**[[10]](https://aimultiple.com/code-execution-with-mcp)[[11]](https://www.getmaxim.ai/articles/code-execution-with-mcp-how-code-mode-cuts-agent-token-costs-by-90/)

- **AI Multiple / related benchmarks (2026)**: “Code execution with MCP” (hybrid approach using Python orchestration/code mode on top of MCP) vs. regular MCP tool calling. Results: 100% success rate both; ~78.5% input token reduction (15,417 → 3,310 avg input tokens) and ~77.4% total token savings with code mode; slight latency increase (+7%). Scales with more tools/servers.[[10]](https://aimultiple.com/code-execution-with-mcp)

- **Code Mode benchmarks (getmaxim.ai / similar, 2026)**: Across rounds with increasing tool counts (96→508 tools): 58–92.8% input token reduction (e.g., 75.1M → 5.4M tokens at largest scale), 55.7–92.2% cost reduction, 100% pass rate. MCP replaces direct tool calls with Python orchestration for massive savings while preserving access.[[11]](https://www.getmaxim.ai/articles/code-execution-with-mcp-how-code-mode-cuts-agent-token-costs-by-90/)

- **CLI/code-like vs. MCP comparisons (multiple 2026 sources)**: CLI approaches (e.g., `gh` GitHub CLI or generated CLIs from MCP specs) often show 92–94% token savings on repeated calls vs. full MCP tool definitions in context; lower initialization cost (near-zero vs. ~55k tokens for large MCP sets); better for composability (piping, loops) but may require sandboxes or skills. One framework notes CLI Token Efficiency Score advantage (202.1 vs. 152.3 for MCP in browser automation). Some tasks slightly favor MCP on latency/cost, but pattern favors code/CLI for scale.[[12]](https://lalatenduswain.medium.com/cli-based-agents-vs-mcp-the-2026-showdown-that-every-ai-engineer-needs-to-understand-7dfbc9e3e1f9)[[13]](https://manveerc.substack.com/p/mcp-vs-cli-ai-agents)[[14]](https://vensas.de/en/blog/mcp-vs-cli-cost-comparison)

- Broader agent leaderboards (e.g., Terminal-Bench, SWE-bench) reference MCP-compatible vs. terminal/code-first agents but focus more on model performance than direct head-to-heads.[[15]](https://www.morphllm.com/best-ai-coding-agents-2026)

These are primarily from X (recent August 2026 activity around Lu’s post and Prime Agent), supplemented by 2026 blogs/benchmarks on code-mode hybrids. MCP proponents stress structured benefits for enterprise/security; bearish views center on models’ native code strengths for efficiency and expressiveness. For deeper dives, check the linked X threads and benchmark articles.
